Command-Line Interface

clip.py exposes the core IFU Analyzer pipeline as a standalone command-line tool. It is useful for scripting, batch jobs, headless servers, and Jupyter workflows where the GUI is not available.

The same code paths used by the GUI are exposed here, so the CLI and the GUI are guaranteed to produce identical results given identical inputs.

Setup

Run clip.py from the project root, one level above cube_explorer/:

python clip.py <command> [options]

If you see ImportError: Could not import CubeData, move clip.py one directory level up so it sits next to main.py.

Commands

Five subcommands are available. Click any of them to jump to its full reference page.

Command

Purpose

auto-continuum

Automatic continuum detection and export

custom-continuum

Continuum fit from user-supplied anchor points

subtract-continuum

Subtract a continuum (constant, fitted file, or anchor points)

2d-rotate

Rotate a 2D FITS image, updating the WCS

2d-contour

Extract contour coordinates from a 2D FITS image

auto-continuum

python clip.py auto-continuum -i <cube.fits> [-p window sigma width distance exclusion iters smoothing]

Automatically fit the continuum baseline of a cube’s integrated spectrum using median filtering, peak detection, iterative sigma clipping, and spline smoothing. The fitted continuum is saved to a tab-delimited ASCII file with header # Type: fitted_continuum, ready to be fed back into subtract-continuum.

The algorithm runs in four steps:

  1. Median filtering of width window produces a first-pass continuum estimate.

  2. Peak detection finds emission/absorption features above sigma × RMS using scipy.signal.find_peaks with the given width and distance constraints.

  3. Iterative sigma clipping removes outliers above the running continuum estimate for iters passes.

  4. Spline smoothing fits a cubic UnivariateSpline to the cleaned continuum with smoothing parameter s = N / smoothing_factor.

After fitting, you are prompted for an output filename. The file is written as <name>.txt in the current directory.

Parameters:
-i, –inputstr

Path to the input FITS cube. Required.

-p, –paramslist of 7 numbers, optional

Algorithm parameters in this exact order: window sigma width distance exclusion iters smoothing. Defaults to 51 2.0 1 3 3 2 5 if omitted.

  • window (int, default 51) — Median-filter window size in channels. Larger values produce a smoother baseline but may miss fine structure. Must be odd. Typical range 21–101.

  • sigma (float, default 2.0) — Peak-detection threshold in units of the RMS. Lower values detect weaker lines. Use 1.5 for clean data, 2.0 for typical, 3.0 for noisy.

  • width (int, default 1) — Minimum width in channels for a feature to count as a peak. Filters out single-channel spikes.

  • distance (int, default 3) — Minimum separation in channels between detected peaks.

  • exclusion (int, default 3) — Channels masked on each side of every detected peak before the final fit. Use larger values for broad lines.

  • iters (int, default 2) — Number of sigma-clipping passes after the first fit.

  • smoothing (int, default 5) — Spline smoothing factor. Smoothness scales as s = N / smoothing_factor. Lower → closer fit to the data; higher → smoother curve.

Output file format:

Tab-delimited ASCII with a comment header:

# Export from IFU-Analyzer CLI
# Instrument: MIRI
# Type: fitted_continuum
# Wavelength unit: micron
# Flux unit: MJy/sr
#
# Wavelength (micron)   Continuum_Fit
6.530400e+00            1.420169e+06
6.531200e+00            1.448846e+06
...

The # Type: fitted_continuum line lets subtract-continuum auto-detect this format on re-import.

Examples:

Default parameters:

python clip.py auto-continuum -i data/miri_cube.fits

Custom parameters — larger window, tighter sigma, more exclusion:

python clip.py auto-continuum -i data/miri_cube.fits -p 75 1.5 2 5 5 3 8

custom-continuum

python clip.py custom-continuum -i <cube.fits> -p <points.csv>

Fit a cubic spline through user-supplied wavelength/flux anchor points, then subtract the result from the spectrum. The output is a 4-column ASCII file in # Type: full_results format — identical to the GUI’s Save Results button.

Parameters:
-i, –inputstr

Path to the input FITS cube. Required.

-p, –pointsstr

Path to a CSV file of anchor points, one per line, comma-separated, no header. Required.

Points file format:
3.5e-6,0.012
4.0e-6,0.015
4.8e-6,0.011

The spline is fit with bc_type='natural' and evaluated at every wavelength channel.

Output file format:
# Type: full_results
# Wavelength (micron)   Original    Continuum    Subtracted
6.530400e+00            1.420169e+06   1.450957e+06   -3.078756e+04
...
Example:
python clip.py custom-continuum -i data/muse_cube.fits -p my_points.csv

subtract-continuum

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i <cube.fits> -c <value_or_file>

Subtract a continuum from a cube’s spectrum. The continuum source is auto-detected from the -c argument:

  • a plain number → constant offset

  • a file with header # Type: fitted_continuum → 2-column file (auto-continuum output)

  • a file with header # Type: full_results → 4-column file (GUI Save Results or CLI custom-continuum output)

  • any other text file → parsed as raw anchor points (wavelength, flux), fit with a cubic spline

Parameters:
-i, –inputstr

Path to the input FITS cube. Required.

-c, –continuumstr or float

One of:

  • A numeric constant (e.g. 0.05). Subtracted from every channel.

  • Path to a fitted_continuum file. The 2-column data is interpolated onto the cube’s wavelength grid and subtracted.

  • Path to a full_results file. The continuum column (3rd column) is extracted, interpolated, and subtracted. Added in the 2026-05 update to support GUI ↔ CLI round-trips.

  • Path to a raw points file. Fit with a cubic spline and subtracted.

Output file format:

Same 4-column # Type: full_results format as custom-continuum.

Examples:

Constant baseline:

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/alma_cube.fits -c 0.03

Re-use a previously fitted continuum:

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/alma_cube.fits -c continuum_export.txt

Re-use a GUI-saved results file (4-column format):

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/cube.fits -c gui_results.txt

Subtract using raw anchor points:

python clip.py subtract-continuum -i data/nirspec_cube.fits -c my_baseline_points.csv

2d-rotate

python clip.py 2d-rotate -i <image.fits> -a <angle_degrees>

Rotate a 2D FITS image and update the WCS CD matrix so RA/Dec coordinates remain accurate after rotation.

Parameters:
-i, –inputstr

Path to the input 2D FITS file. Required.

-a, –anglefloat

Rotation angle in degrees, positive = counter-clockwise. Required.

Notes:

  • scipy.ndimage.rotate is used with reshape=True and cval=NaN (empty border pixels are NaN, not zero).

  • The CD matrix update is CD_new = CD_orig × R⁻¹ where R is the 2D rotation matrix for -angle.

  • CRPIX is not changed — the reference pixel stays at the same sky coordinate.

Output:

A new FITS file with the rotated image and updated WCS header. You are prompted for the output filename.

Example:
python clip.py 2d-rotate -i data/miri_intensity.fits -a 45

2d-contour

python clip.py 2d-contour -i <image.fits> -l <level1> [level2 ...]

Generate contour lines at user-specified sigma levels and save every vertex’s pixel and sky coordinates to a text file.

Parameters:
-i, –inputstr

Path to the input 2D FITS file. Required.

-l, –levelslist of float

Sigma multipliers, space-separated. Each level N draws a contour at median + N × RMS where median and RMS are from astropy.stats.sigma_clipped_stats (3σ clipping). Required, at least one value.

Output file format:

Comma-separated ASCII:

# IFU Analyzer 2D - Contour Export
# level, x_pixel, y_pixel, RA_deg, Dec_deg
3.000000e+00, 42.1234, 18.7654, 67.90591, 18.20682
...

You are prompted for the output filename.

Examples:

Single level:

python clip.py 2d-contour -i data/moment0.fits -l 3

Multiple levels:

python clip.py 2d-contour -i data/moment0.fits -l 3 5 10 20

Using the CLI from Jupyter

clip.py exposes the same five commands as plain Python functions, specifically for use from Jupyter notebooks or scripts. They take output_name as a keyword argument, skipping the interactive filename prompt that the CLI uses.

from clip import (
    auto_continuum,
    custom_continuum,
    subtract_continuum,
    rotate_2d,
    contour_2d,
)

auto_continuum("mycube.fits", output_name="continuum_out")
subtract_continuum("mycube.fits", "continuum_out.txt", output_name="subtracted")
custom_continuum("mycube.fits", "points.csv", output_name="custom_sub")
rotate_2d("image.fits", 45, output_name="rotated_45")
contour_2d("image.fits", [3, 5, 10], output_name="contours")

All five wrappers accept output_name=None (the default), in which case the function falls back to the same interactive input() prompt the CLI uses.

Troubleshooting

Jupyter notebook issues

Cell hangs after running a CLI command with !python clip.py ...

Jupyter does not forward keyboard input to ! subprocesses, so when clip.py calls input() for the output filename, it sits waiting for input that will never arrive.

Fix: pipe the filename in via echo, or use the Python wrapper functions:

# Option A — pipe the filename
!echo my_output | python clip.py auto-continuum -i cube.fits

# Option B — use the wrapper (recommended)
from clip import auto_continuum
auto_continuum("cube.fits", output_name="my_output")

FileNotFoundError when loading the FITS file

Jupyter’s working directory is wherever Jupyter was started, not where the FITS file lives. Either start Jupyter from the project folder, or change directory inside the notebook:

import os
os.chdir(r"C:\path\to\IFU-Analyzer")

Then verify with os.path.exists("mycube.fits").

ImportError: cannot import CubeData

clip.py must be at the project root, one level above cube_explorer/. The wrapper expects to be importable as from cube_explorer.data_loader import CubeData.

Fix: move clip.py up one level if it is currently inside cube_explorer/.

Filename contains a space or parenthesis

The shell splits on spaces, so a filename like Level3_ch1-long_s3d (1).fits is parsed as two arguments.

Fix: quote the path, or rename the file:

python clip.py auto-continuum -i "Level3_ch1-long_s3d (1).fits"

CLI issues

“unrecognized arguments”

Almost always caused by an unquoted filename containing spaces. See the previous item.

The continuum file from the GUI is not recognized

The CLI accepts both legacy fitted_continuum (2 columns) and the new full_results (4 columns) formats out of the box. If you still get a parse error, open the file in a text editor and confirm it has either # Type: fitted_continuum or # Type: full_results in the first 15 lines.

“–params expects 7 values”

auto-continuum’s --params flag requires all seven values in order, even if you only want to change one. Use the default block 51 2.0 1 3 3 2 5 as a starting template and edit the values you need.

Output file has fewer rows than the cube’s wavelength channels

The continuum output (fitted_continuum format) only writes rows where the fit was finite. NaN regions of the spectrum are skipped. The 4-column full_results output preserves every channel, writing nan where appropriate.

Cube loads but the spectrum looks wrong

clip.py uses CubeData from cube_explorer.data_loader, which computes cube.spectrum as the mean across all spatial pixels. If you need a region-restricted spectrum, use the GUI’s region tools to define the region first, then save the spectrum from the GUI.
